Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:11:1.hebrew: דמקני ליה כפילא - הבעלים מקנין לשומר כפל העתיד להשתלם, כדאמר לקמן, שבשעה שמסרה לו לשמור על מנת כן מסרה, שאם תגנב וירצה וישלם, יהא כפל שלו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:11:1.english: That [the owner] transfers to him the double payment - The owners transfer to the bailee the double [payment] that will be paid in the future, as [the Gemara] says below, that at the time he handed it over to him to guard, he handed it over on this condition: that if it is stolen and he chooses to pay, the double [payment] shall be his.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:11:2.english: Say [that] he does not transfer the double payment to him - He did not hand it over to him initially on that condition.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:12:1.hebrew: דלא נפיש כפלייהו - שאין באין לידי ארבעה וחמשה, שאינה נוהגת אלא בשור ושה בלבד:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:12:1.english: That their double payment is not substantial - For they do not come to [the liability of] fourfold and fivefold [payment], as it applies only to an ox and a sheep alone.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:13:1.english: Rami objects to it, etc. - He is raising a difficulty on the Mishnah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:13:2.hebrew: והא אין אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם - והיאך הקנו לו בעלים כפל זה, שעדיין לא נתחייב בו גנב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:13:2.english: But a person cannot transfer ownership of something that has not come into the world - And how did the owners transfer to him this double [payment], for which the thief had not yet become liable?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:13:3.hebrew: ואפילו לר' מאיר דאמר - בפ"ג דקדושין (דף סג.): הרי את מקודשת לי על מנת שאתגייר, איכא למיגמר מינה מוכר פירות דקל לחבירו עד שלא באו לעולם, דאפליגו בה רב הונא ורב נחמן לקמן באיזהו נשך (בבא מציעא דף סו:):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:13:3.english: And even according to Rabbi Meir, who says - In the third chapter of Kiddushin (63a): "Behold, you are betrothed to me on condition that I convert" — from it one can derive [the case of] one who sells the fruits of a date palm to his fellow before they have come into the world, regarding which Rav Huna and Rav Nachman disagreed later in [the chapter] Eizehu Neshech (Bava Metzia 66b).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:13:4.english: Which are likely to come - [This is] our reading.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:1:1.hebrew: בימי רבי נשנית משנה זו - הא דקתני "תלמוד אין לך מדה גדולה מזו" — לפי שמשרבו תלמידי שמאי והלל, שהיו לפניו שלשה דורות, רבו מחלוקות בתורה ונעשית כשתי תורות, מתוך עול שעבוד מלכיות וגזירות שהיו גוזרין עליהן. ומתוך כך לא היו יכולים לתת לב לברר דברי החולקים עד ימיו של רבי, שנתן הקב"ה לו חן בעיני אנטונינוס מלך רומי — כדאמרינן בעבודה זרה (דף י.) — ונחו מצרה. ושלח וקבץ כל תלמידי ארץ ישראל. ועד ימיו לא היו מסכתות סדורות, אלא כל תלמיד ששמע דבר מפי גדול הימנו גרסה ונתן סימנים: "הלכה פלונית ופלונית שמעתי משם פלוני". וכשנתקבצו, אמר כל אחד מה ששמע, ונתנו לב לברר טעמי המחלוקת, דברי מי ראוין לקיים, וסידרו המסכתות: דברי נזיקין לבדם, ודברי יבמות לבדם, ודברי קדשים לבדם. וסתם נמי במשנה דברי יחידים, שראה רבי את דבריהם ושנאן סתם כדי לקבוע הלכה כמותם. לפיכך אמרו בגמרא: "אין לך מדה גדולה מזו", שיתנו לב לטעמי המשנה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:1:1.english: During the days of Rabbi this mishnah was taught - [Regarding] that which it teaches, "Talmud — there is no greater measure than it" — [it was taught] because from the time the disciples of Shammai and Hillel increased, who were three generations before him, disputes multiplied in the Torah and it became like two Torahs, due to the yoke of subjugation to [foreign] kingdoms and the decrees that they would decree upon them. And because of this, they were unable to pay attention to clarify the words of those who disagreed until the days of Rabbi, when the Holy One, Blessed be He, granted him favor in the eyes of Antoninus, king of Rome — as we say in Avodah Zarah (10a) — and they rested from distress. And [Rabbi] sent [word] and gathered all the scholars of the Land of Israel. Until his days, the tractates were not arranged [in order]; rather, each scholar who heard a matter from the mouth of one greater than himself memorized it and made mnemonic signs: "Such-and-such a halakhah and such-and-such [a halakhah] I heard in the name of so-and-so." And when they gathered, each one stated what he had heard, and they paid attention to clarify the reasons behind the disputes, [determining] whose words were fitting to uphold, and they arranged the tractates: matters of damages by themselves, matters of levirate marriage by themselves, and matters of consecrated [offerings] by themselves. And he also taught anonymously in the Mishnah the statements of individuals whose words Rabbi approved and taught anonymously in order to establish the halakhah in accordance with them. Therefore they said in the Gemara, "There is no greater measure than it," [meaning] that they should pay attention to the reasons of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:1:2.hebrew: שבקו כולי עלמא מתני' - מלחזור על גרסת משנתם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:1:2.english: Everyone abandoned the Mishnah - [They ceased] from reviewing the text of their Mishnah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:1:3.english: And they pursued the Talmud - To think with [logical] reasoning.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:1:4.hebrew: הדר דרש להו הוי רץ למשנה - לפי שירא פן ישתכחו המשניות, ויחליפו שמות החכמים, ובמקום חיוב יאמרו פטור, ובמקום אסור יאמרו מותר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:1:4.english: He then expounded to them: Run to [the study of] the Mishnah - Because he feared lest the Mishnayot be forgotten, and they confuse the names of the Sages, and in place of liable they say exempt, and in place of prohibited they say permitted.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:2:1.english: What did they expound - Originally, when he expounded that [the study of] Gemara is great.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:2:2.hebrew: לעמי פשעם - עמי, דהיינו ת"ח, את חטאתם אני קורא פשע, שהיה להם לתת לב בטעמי משנתם שיבררו להם על העיקר, ולא יורו הלכה מתוך משנה שאינה עיקר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:2:2.english: To My people their transgression - My people — that is, Torah scholars — their sins I call "transgression," because they should have paid attention to the reasons of their Mishnah so that they would clarify for themselves [what is] the primary [halakhah], and not rule halakhah from a Mishnah that is not primary.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:2:3.english: And to the house of Jacob - [This refers to] the rest of the people.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:2:4.english: Their sins - Even their transgression I call an [unwitting] sin.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:3:1.hebrew: הוי זהיר בתלמוד - בגמרא שהוא תירוץ [טעמי] המשניות, או אם תשמע דבר משנה מרבך, הזהר לשאול טעמיו ומי שנאה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:3:1.english: Be careful in [the study of] the Talmud - In the Gemara, which is the explanation of the reasons for the mishnayot; or if you hear a mishnaic teaching from your teacher, be careful to ask its reasons and who taught it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:3:2.hebrew: שגגת תלמוד - אם שגית בהוראה בשגגת תלמודך, שלא ידעת טעם המשנה ונתת בה טעם אחר, ומתוך כך דמית לה דין או הוראה שבא לידך ולמדת הימנה שלא כדת, שאין הטעם כמו שהיית סבור; שאילו ידעת טעם המשנה, לא דמית לה מעשה הבא לידך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:3:2.english: An unwitting error in study - If you erred in [issuing] a ruling through an unwitting error in your study, in that you did not know the reason of the Mishnah and attributed a different reason to it, and as a result you compared to it a case or a ruling that came before you and derived [a decision] from it not in accordance with the law, since the reason is not as you had thought; for had you known the reason of the Mishnah, you would not have compared the case that came before you to it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:3:3.hebrew: עולה זדון - ענוש אתה עליה כמזיד, שזדון הוא בידך שלא שאלת טעם מרבך:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:3:3.english: Is considered an intentional [transgression] - You are punished for it as an intentional [transgressor], for it is an intentional [act] on your part, in that you did not ask the reason from your teacher.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:4:1.hebrew: אלו ת"ח - ששימשו חכמים הרבה ללמדם טעמי משנתם, זה בזו וזה בזו, שאין הכל בקיאין בשוין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:4:1.english: These are Torah scholars - Who served many sages [for the sages] to teach them the reasons of their Mishnah, this [sage] in this [matter] and that [sage] in that [matter], for not all are equally expert.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:4:2.hebrew: שנאיכם אלו בעלי משנה - ששונאין בעלי גמרא, לפי שבעלי גמרא אומרים על בעלי משנה שהן מבלי עולם, כדאמרינן במסכת סוטה (דף כב.): התנאים מבלי עולם, שמורים הלכה מתוך משנתם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:4:2.english: That hate you — these are masters of Mishna - For they hate the masters of Gemara, because the masters of Gemara say about the masters of Mishna that they are destroyers of the world, as we say in Tractate Sotah (22a): "The Tannaim [reciters of Mishna] are destroyers of the world, for they rule on halakha [directly] from their Mishna."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:4:3.hebrew: מנדיכם אלו ע"ה - שת"ח שנואין ומתועבין להן כנדה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:4:3.english: “That ostracize you” — these are ignoramuses - For Torah scholars are hated and abhorrent to them like a menstruant woman [niddah].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:5:1.hebrew: שמא תאמר אבד סברם - של אלו, שהרי כתיב "למען שמי יכבד ה'", דמשמע שהם אומרים, אבל אין הדבר כן:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:5:1.english: Lest you say their hope is lost - Of these [people], for it is written, "For My name's sake let the Lord be glorified," which implies that they are saying [this], but the matter is not so.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:5:2.hebrew: ת"ל ונראה בשמחתכם - ולא נאמר ואראה בשמחתכם; כך אמר הנביא: אני ואחיכם שונאיכם ומנדיכם — כולנו נראה בשמחתכם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:5:2.english: The verse states: “That we may gaze upon your joy” - And it does not say “That I may gaze upon your joy.” Thus said the prophet: I, and your brothers, those who hate you, and those who cast you out — all of us will gaze upon your joy.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:5:3.hebrew: והם יבושו - אותם שהם עובדי כוכבים, שאינם ממנו ואינן נקראין על שם ישראל, יבושו, וישראל ישמחו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:5:3.english: But they shall be ashamed - Those who are idolaters, who are not of us and are not called by the name of Israel, will be ashamed, and Israel will rejoice.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:7:1.hebrew: המפקיד. ולא רצה לישבע - שבועת שומרים שלא פשע בה ושלא שלח בה יד, שהיה יכול ליפטר בשבועה זו, שהרי אמרו כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:7:1.english: One who deposits. And he did not wish to take an oath - [That is,] the oath of bailees, that he was not negligent with it and did not lay a hand on it; for he could have been exempted [from liability] through this oath, as [the Sages] said, etc.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:8:1.hebrew: למי שהפקדון אצלו - דכיון דשילם, קנה כל תשלומיה, ובגמרא מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 33b:8:1.english: To the one with whom the deposit is - For since [the bailee] paid, he acquired all payments for it, and in the Gemara [the] reason is explained.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33b:13:1.hebrew: כגון פירות דקל דעבידי דאתו - וא"ת: והכא, אפילו אי עבידי דאתו, היאך יקנה הכפל במעות ששילם? והלא מעות אינן קונות, אלא למיקם עליה במי שפרע? ועוד, מאי קפריך בסמוך "מי יימר דמיגנבא"? והלא כששילם כבר נגנבה, והול"ל "מי יימר דנגנבה" — פירוש: שכבר נגנבה, שמא נאבדה. ויש לומר, דהמקשה סבר דבשעת משיכה הקנה לו הפרה לקנות הכפל כשיבא; ואע"ג דבפרק מי שמת (ב"ב דף קמז:) אמרי' דבדקל לפירות אפילו רבנן מודו דקני — היינו משום דעבידי דאתו, אבל הכא דלא עבידו דאתא, אפילו לר' מאיר לא קני. וקשה: דבפ' השולח (גיטין מב: ושם) מיבעיא לן בעבד שמכרו רבו לקנס, דדילמא אפילו לר' מאיר לא יועיל משום דלא עבידא דאתי דמנגח, או דילמא אפילו לרבנן יועיל משום דהא קאי עבדא והוי כדקל לפירותיו; והכא פשיטא ליה דלא מהני פרה לכפילא ואפילו לר"מ! וי"ל, דשמא התם שכיח טפי מהכא; אי נמי, הכא פריך אם תימצי לומר בעבד שמכרו רבו לקנס דלא מהני לר"מ. ומשני: "נעשה כאומר לו לכשתגנב ותשלמני הרי פרתי קנויה לך מעכשיו" — שגוף הפרה מכר לו, דהשתא הכפל שלו ממילא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33b:13:1.english: "Such as the fruits of a date palm, which are likely to come" - And if you ask: Here, even if they were likely to come [into existence], how could he acquire the double payment through the money that he paid? Do not money [payments] not effect acquisition, except to subject him to [the curse of] mi shepara? And furthermore, why does [the Gemara] object shortly after, "Who says that it will be stolen?" When he paid, it had already been stolen, and it should have said, "Who says that it was stolen?" — meaning: [even if you know] that it was already stolen, perhaps it was [merely] lost! And one can say that the questioner thought that at the time of meshikhah [when the bailee took possession], [the owner] transferred the cow to him in order to acquire the double payment when it comes; and even though in the chapter Mi SheMet (Bava Batra 147b) we say that regarding a palm tree [sold] for its fruit even the Rabbis agree that he acquires [it], that is because [the fruits] are likely to come, whereas here, since [the double payment] is not likely to come, even according to Rabbi Meir he does not acquire [it]. And this is difficult: for in the chapter HaSholeach (Gittin 42b and elsewhere), we have an inquiry regarding a slave whose master sold him for his [potential] fine [kenas]: perhaps even according to Rabbi Meir it will not avail because it is not likely to happen that [an ox] will gore [him], or perhaps even according to the Rabbis it will avail because the slave is standing [here in existence] and is like a palm tree [sold] for its fruit; yet here [Rami bar Hama] is certain that [transferring] a cow does not avail for the double payment, even according to Rabbi Meir! And one can say that perhaps there [an ox goring] is more common than here; alternatively, here he objects [assuming] "if you conclude and say" regarding a slave whose master sold him for his fine that it does not avail according to Rabbi Meir. And [Rava] answers: "It is as though he said to him: 'When it is stolen and you pay me, my cow is hereby acquired by you from now'" — for he sold him the body of the cow [itself], so that now the double payment is his automatically:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33b:4:1.hebrew: אחיכם אלו בעלי מקרא - שאינם יודעים דינים והוראות כי אם על פי בעלי גמרא. שונאיכם אלו בעלי משנה — שסבורים לידע כמו בעלי גמרא, ואינם יודעים בירור הדבר. מנדיכם אלו ע"ה, ששונאים ת"ח. ושמא תאמר: אבד סברן? ת"ל: "ונראה בשמחתכם" — ישראל ישמחו, ועובדי כוכבים יבושו:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33b:4:1.english: "Your brothers" — these are masters of Scripture - For they do not know laws and legal rulings except through the masters of the Gemara. "That hate you" — these are masters of Mishnah, who think they know [as much] as the masters of the Gemara, yet do not know the clarification of the matter. "That ostracize you" — these are ignoramuses, who hate Torah scholars. And lest you say, "Their hope is lost," the verse teaches: "that we may gaze upon your joy" — Israel will rejoice, and the idolaters will be ashamed.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33b:7:1.hebrew: המפקיד - אית דלא גרסי "או שאבדו", משום דבאבידה ליכא כפל. ויש ליישב, שכך טוען הנפקד ואחר כך נמצא הגנב; אי נמי: אנו יודעים שנגנבו מתוך ביתו, אך אין אנו יודעים אם פשע; "או שאבדו" — שאנו יודעין שנאבד ממנו, אך לא ידעינן אם על ידי גניבה או על ידי דבר אחר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33b:7:1.english: One who deposits - There are those who do not have the reading "or they were lost," because for a lost item there is no double payment. And it can be reconciled [as follows]: that this is what the bailee claims, and afterward the thief is found. Alternatively: we know that they were stolen from his house, yet we do not know whether he was negligent; [and] "or they were lost" [means] that we know it was lost from him, yet we do not know whether through theft or through something else.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33b:7:2.hebrew: נגנבו - ה"ה אם אמר "פשעתי", שהכפל שלו, כדאמר בגמרא: מגו דאי בעי פטר נפשיה בגניבה. אלא אורחא דמילתא נקט "נגנבו", שהוא רגילות לטעון דבר שהוא פטור, אע"פ שהוא רוצה לשלם. וריב"ן פי' דמתני' נמי ה"פ: דהנפקד אומר שנגנבו בפשיעה, ו"לא רצה לישבע" היינו ולא רצה לישבע לשקר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 33b:7:2.english: They were stolen - The same law applies if he said, "I was negligent" — that the double payment belongs to him, as [the Gemara] says: since if he wanted, he could have exempted himself with [a claim of] theft. Rather, [the Tanna] used the common manner of speaking [when he stated] "they were stolen," for it is customary to claim something for which one is exempt, even though he wants to pay. And Rivan explained that our Mishnah as well means as follows: that the bailee says that they were stolen through negligence, and "he did not wish to take an oath" means: he did not wish to swear falsely.
